sourceAttributionBeforeImplementation:
# Source cost attribution — before production optimization

Baseline HEAD e774553df / frozen 21.1.250.59-beta. This file precedes any production source modification in this stage.

## Exact call chain

1. RegionThreadingEngine.tickFurnaceWorkWaves publishes lifecycle batch, creates canonical ordered admissions, runs whole-phase inventory alias audit.
2. One FurnaceWorkPreparation per initial pass. For each candidate, fresh binding/source/chunk/block-state/3-slot item/notification checks. pureCatalog once per *present cooking type in this pass*, not once per furnace; full current recipe/ingredient/result/component audit.
3. Resource ON additionally builds SharedReads identity publication, FurnaceResourcePreparation local Binding/Identity/slot predicates, immutable Claims and conservative fences. OFF creates its existing BlockEntityWorkPlanner footprint objects.
4. Resource plan performs complete phase home/global WRITE alias audit and canonical directed dependency planning. Initial plan is advisory, not a reservation.
5. Canonical serial fences run in place. Each multi-unit wave takes outer Region leases in canonical order and delivers mailboxes, then performs a *new* FurnaceWorkPreparation and whole-phase inventory alias audit. No prior catalog success is reused.
6. ON builds fresh local Claims, compares captured normalized permissions, then tryAcquireAll independently checks complete budgets, current homes/READ-WRITE conflicts/every ordinary Binding validator/each distinct shared predicate; rechecks level lifecycle and held homes. Only then one-shot leases/scopes publish bodies.
7. Join every worker, canonical setChanged commits, close resource ownership, release Region leases; failed effects never replay. fullPhase also includes serial BE execution, Region leasing/mailboxes/barrier/cleanup and lifecycle overhead.

## Counts already verified from original accepted receipts

- Standard mixed r0 regions: 600 exact ticks, 600 furnace waves, 38376 native bodies, 28824 serial BE ticks. Thus one multi-unit wave/tick despite 48 unknown serial BE fences. Must not attribute its ~3.6MB/s resource delta to many worker dispatches.
- Pipeline: one multi-unit wave/tick too; Hopper-fenced individual furnaces are serial. Their initial candidate/claim preparation has cost but deleting/reordering the fences would violate canonical effects.
- Multiple-wave tests remain important: inter-wave serial callbacks can mutate recipe results/components/inventory/chunk/ticker, so every later wave needs a fresh catalog + phase-alias audit. No safe general invalidation hook currently covers arbitrary unknown callback writes.

## Source-level allocations, with responsibilities kept distinct

- AbstractCookingRecipe.getIngredients() creates NonNullList + ArrayList + element storage per recipe. RecipeManager.getAllRecipesFor returns List.copyOf current type collection. Both ON/OFF pay these each fresh pass; this is not automatically the ON/OFF increment.
- Ingredient.getValues and getItems return current stored arrays once lazy caches resolve; do not falsely count a new array for each getValues call. CompoundIngredient descendants must be audited/captured separately because merged caches deduplicate equal stacks.
- Resource ON catalog capture creates identity set, publication list, SharedReads identity array and lookup index. This is extra vs OFF, but results/components and all child identities must remain fresh.
- Each local Claims capture creates Builder, temporary arrays, Binding/Identity/predicates, detached binding and normalized permission arrays. This repeats for plan and fresh validation even when all local identities/attachments are unchanged within the phase.
- Whole-phase plan and fresh reservation each allocate ResourceTable keys/homes/flags. Reader/writer depths are planning only. Reusing a zeroed scratch table could save capacity without retaining any successful proof or occupancy.
- Core lease state CAS, thread binding, active-scope/lifecycle/home checks and current READ/WRITE reservation are semantic enforcement, not removable bookkeeping.

## Candidate boundaries (not yet accepted until JFR comparison)

- Share immutable local descriptor arrays within one phase only when fresh candidate source/chunk/all three slot references match. Still construct a new fresh shared publication, compare normalized captured sets, and run all local attachment validators in reservation. Full recapture for changed slots preserves accepted permutations and conservatively refuses replacement resources.
- Reuse only identity-table capacity inside one coordinator-owned phase, clearing every key/home/flag on every exit including refusal/throw. Independently recompute aliases, conflicts and current proofs. No table state used as permission authority.
- Catalog API wrapper allocations may be visible in absolute cost but a separate API/Vanilla patch change needs evidence. Do not add broad caching to avoid current recipe traversal.

JFR baseline ON/OFF and its independent primary performance measurements remain separate. Allocation weights are sampled, not exact per-method bytes; wall segment timers overlap/nest and cannot sum to native full-tick MSPT.

chosen: Same-phase immutable local descriptor reuse only after fresh source/chunk/all three slot identities match; otherwise full recapture. New shared publication and all reservation validators always retained.
Same-phase coordinator-owned scratch identity table capacity; every key/home/flag cleared on all success/refusal/throw exits; all current alias/conflict checks recomputed.
notChosen: Do not cache catalog audit outcomes across passes/waves/ticks. Unknown serial callbacks lack a complete invalidation protocol.
Do not merge/reorder serial fences. Standard mixed workload has one worker wave/tick, so repeated dispatch is not its primary resource delta.
Do not add Vanilla recipe APIs in this iteration: catalog wrapper traversal is common OFF/ON cost; first reduce directly measured resource-specific representation allocation.

excludedValidationAttempts.reason: buildSrc lacks root immaculate extension; guarded :tests project before rerunning
test in production package created a FML Java module split package; moved to unittest/reflection without changing production API

Source review found same-reference zero-count stack can become nonempty; added captured empty/nonempty mask and a regression. First queue stopped gracefully in profile60 OFF. All first-candidate data archived under exploration-v1 and excluded; final corrected matrix rerun.

methodology: Independent JVM rounds reported separately, both condition and build order reversed.
JFR profiles, dynamic reload/unload and correctness-only Hopper pipeline excluded from primary performance matrices.
Mean/p50/p95/p99/max, allocation and GC include all accepted windows and tails; no success filtering.
Scratch shares capacity only within one phase; immutable local descriptors are not successful current proofs.
MXBean collection time is not total STW/GC CPU; JFR weights and sample counts are not exact method allocations/times.
New soak is 10 active minutes/condition with quiescent refill checkpoints; prior 30-minute baseline is linked, not counted as rerun.
No players/active AI/modpack saturation or arbitrary asynchronous mutation support claimed.

removedRepresentationCosts: Second local Binding/Identity/predicate/normalized-array construction for unchanged same-phase attachments and captured nonempty membership.
Second allocation of identity-table capacity for reservation; every call recomputes all checks and clears every key/home/flag.
preservedSemanticCosts: Fresh catalog/ingredients/OR children/results/components and notification audit after every required region/mailbox boundary.
Full-phase current inventory alias audit, current attachment checks, directed ordering, whole-wave READ/WRITE and home reservation.
One-shot lease/thread-bound scope, lifecycle/current boundary checks, canonical unknown serial fences, joins/commits and no replay.
remainingImplementationCosts: Initial Claims/Binding/Identity/arrays and catalog wrapper/publication allocations.
Dependency depth arrays, table probes/clearing, owner/boundary maps and Lease/Scope wrappers.

A reused phase-sized table can exceed a later small wave's needed capacity; full flags scans/clearing may cost more CPU than a right-sized table. Allocation reduction is not equivalent to guaranteed latency reduction; eight-wave negative latency retained.
conclusions.asyncReloadException: Dynamic fifth window has different before-state/route: native10785/10786, serial11615/11614, changes39/40. Both sides exact22400 tickable BE bodies and complete bounded legal effects/UUID/holder audit pass; no unique causal or full-pair equality claim.
conclusions.exploratoryFirstCandidateExcluded: Source review found in-place zero-count stack becoming nonempty; captured nonempty mask and regression added before final full rerun.
conclusions.interpretation: Source and JFR support lower representation allocation; full-Tick latency varies substantially across same binaries/conditions and early/late windows. Preserve all negative results. No blanket GC/JIT/scheduler/root-lock causal claim or default-on/admission expansion.

host-point-during-slow-matrix.json.limit: One read-only point snapshot during slow windows; not causal evidence for earlier per-tick delays.
